text:
maria: FYI customer Saturn reported a weird token-drop after we merged their LoRA + int4 rollout. Quick eval pack shows truncation mid-answer on a handful of prompts. Anyone seen this pattern before?

aj: Can you paste the eval output and the exact quant config? int4 + fused kernels sometimes exposes tokenizer alignment issues.

dave: tagging @aj — also, did we re-tokenize the LoRA weights with the same tokenizer/version? small vocab shift causes token shifts like this.

maria: Pasting sanitized snippet from the eval pack (shortened):
```
PROMPT: "Explain the tradeoffs of sharded cache in 2 bullets"
REFERENCE: "1) ... 2) ..."
PREDICTED (truncated): "1) Sharding reduces memory but adds network overhead. 2) It can cause" <-- stops here
METRICS: perplexity +8, exact-match 0.0, avg_tokens 12 (expected 22)
CONFIG: model: cust/saturn-7b+lora-2026, quant: int4-gptq, tokenizer: huggingface/tokenizer-v2.1
```

nima: CI-bot ran the smoke tests after merge, no infra or OOMs reported. Dropping tokens smells like tokenizer mismatch or a KV-cache length bug.

aj: Quick checklist: 1) verify tokenizer vocab ids used during LoRA creation vs current runtime 2) run the same input through HF tokenizer locally and compare token counts 3) try int8 or fp16 to see if quantization interacts with the issue

dave: On the HF tokenizer point, we had one case where a space-join change altered tokenization of punctuation. Also check if the merged adapter introduced a decode-time early-stop hack (some custom decode wrappers do this).

maria: I ran local repro with the exact config; here's the tokenized output for the failing prompt:
```
[101, 2356, 879, 34, 4450, 2, 9999, 0, 0]
length: 9
```
That "0" padding in the middle is odd — looks like a broken token id insertion.

aj: Oof. That indicates a bad tokenizer merge or token remap table. Which commit for tokenizer was used?

maria: LoRA was merged with commit `lora/merge-ctlr-aa3f` and tokenizer bump `tokenizer/v2.1+patch` in the same PR. I suspect the tokenizer patch introduced a remap table that our runtime doesn't load for quantized kernels.

nima: I can run a narrow smoke: load model with int8/FP16 and run the exact tokenization path; also will diff tokenizer vocab files between versions. Starting now. :mag:

ci-bot: smoke-run 1777777777 triggered by @nima — logs at https://ci.internal/runs/1777777777 (public access restricted)

aj: Meanwhile, @maria can you create a minimal eval with `--no-cache` and `--force-tokenizer=tokenizer/v2.0` to see if falling back to older tokenizer avoids the drop? That will prove tokenizer delta.

maria: Doing that now. Quick results: with v2.0 tokens length 22, full answer completes. With v2.1 tokens length 9 + padding and truncation persists. So confirms tokenizer change is the culprit.

dave: Great repro. Two remediation options: 1) revert tokenizer patch in the runtime until we properly port the remap table for quantized kernels, or 2) update the LoRA merge process to re-encode the adapter to the new tokenizer (preferred for long term).

aj: For short-term customer mitigation, revert the runtime tokenizer to v2.0 on their dedicated pool (config flag), and push a hotfix to the merge toolchain to re-tokenize adapters during merge.

maria: I'll open an incident-priority PR for runtime rollback + a follow-up task to re-encode the LoRA. Assigning to @dave for the re-encode script and @nima to validate across int4/int8/fp16.

nima: Will validate. I'll also add a quick eval entry to the onboarding pack that explicitly checks token counts vs reference for any tokenizer bumps.

maria: Thanks all — looping Saturn customer ops. Will post update when runtime rollback is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
